A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same graph-connectivity study. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and alignable despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: Sections 3.3 and 5 and Appendix D report original Transformer training experiments, connectivity accuracies, capacity measurements and weight analyses.

after.justification: The original empirical study is retained, with an additional restricted-versus-unrestricted training comparison on two-clique graphs in Figure 11.

M1.justification: The architectures and diameter-based data lever remain unchanged. Theorem 4.9 introduces an analyzed training variant using L2-regularized population risk and projected gradient descent with nonnegative A_l and B_l. This is not reported as a change to the experimental implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions use Erdős–Rényi graphs and two-chain/two-clique evaluations, including the same diameter and edge-probability scenarios. v2 Figure 11 extends the data-lever comparison to two-clique graphs already evaluated in v1; it introduces no new data population or task.

E2.justification: No new baseline algorithm is evaluated. The unrestricted-training control and diameter-restriction variants remain; v2 Figure 11 uses the same restricted-versus-unrestricted comparison already used in Figure 7.

E3.justification: Appendices A and D retain the evaluation metrics, model configurations, sample counts, training budgets and optimizer settings. Figure 11 explicitly follows Figure 7's setup. The new theoretical optimization procedure is not documented as an experimental protocol revision.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 11 adds a controlled robustness check asking whether diameter-restricted training also improves standard Transformers on disconnected cliques. Existing diameter-cutoff, mixture-proportion and training-dynamics analyses remain, including v1 Figure 11 as v2 Figure 12.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Removing the fluctuating traces from Figure 7 changes its display, without documenting a change in statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Figure 11 reports higher two-clique accuracy with restricted training, peaking around 0.4 before declining toward 0.1; unrestricted training remains lower. The principal capacity and two-chain results are retained. Some earlier weight snapshots and the diameter-distribution histogram are omitted.

T1.justification: New Appendix C.5 adds gradient-mapping, coercivity, smoothness and descent arguments for regularized projected gradient descent, with KKT limit-point guarantees and heuristic-suppression corollaries. v2 also formalizes model capacity and sharpens the counterexample construction from diameter greater than 3^L to exactly 3^L+1.

C1.justification: Despite the more assertive title and added theoretical support, the abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: the 3^L capacity threshold, algorithmic/heuristic decomposition, data-dependent learning dynamics and benefits of training within capacity.

C2.justification: Remark C.19 newly qualifies convergence as a statement about limit points rather than a unique limiting solution. Appendix C.5 also explains regularization's roles in bounding iterates and suppressing the heuristic channel, extending the interpretation of the original training-dynamics analysis.

D1.justification: The architecture specification and experimental implementation details are retained, including hidden width, batch sizes, sample counts, learning rates, optimizers and channel-share computation. No new code/data access information, hardware specifications or runtime measurements are supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds optimization references supporting convergence, a GNN message-passing comparison citing Hamilton, and additional chain-of-thought and reasoning literature. It removes several earlier citations, including the NLI examples and Wen et al.'s interpretability caveat. Most mechanistic-interpretability discussion is relocated to Appendix E.

P1.justification: The introduction and contribution presentation are substantially rewritten, and Section 4.3 reorganizes the channel explanations around explicit convergence results. The title changes, mechanistic-interpretability related work moves to Appendix E, and an impact statement is added.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive figure recomposition. Figures 1, 3, 4 and 6 lose panels, Figure 7 retains only the smooth trajectories, and the new two-clique Figure 11 shifts the retained diameter-scaling figure to Figure 12.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful stationarity analysis and two-clique evidence. However, its main-text claim of iterate convergence exceeds Remark C.19's limit-point guarantee, and Corollary C.22 infers full capacity attainment from Lemma C.12's one-sided support bound without establishing the converse. These gaps affect the central theoretical addition, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain.
